subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Honda's Rebel Spirit
description: A short lesson to help you apply Honda's Rebel Spirit.

hook.text: Soichiro Honda failed an engineering exam and never got a degree. He built cars anyway.

buildup.text: He started with motorcycles after the war, making cheap bikes from surplus military engines.

discovery.text: When Honda entered the car market in 1963, Japan's government told him to stop—they had enough carmakers.

twist.text: Honda ignored them. His CVCC engine passed US emissions standards without a catalytic converter.

climax.text: The Civic and Accord became best-sellers in America, built on efficiency and clever engineering.

punchline.text: Honda proved that rebels can outperform empires.

quiz.question: What did Japan's government tell Honda to do?
